title: Book a VIIU inspection for a written-off light vehicle
summary: This page outlines the process for written-off light vehicles to undergo a VIIU inspection before they can be re-registered in NSW.
intro:
Once NSW written-off light vehicles have been repaired, certified by a licensed repairer and inspected under the Authorised Unregistered Vehicle Inspection Scheme (AUVIS), they must then undergo a Vehicle Identity & Inspections Unit (VIIU) inspection before they can be re-registered.

Note: Interstate written-off light vehicles must have been re-registered in another state or territory following the write-off event, before they can be registered in NSW.
who_can_apply: The vehicle must be a written-off light vehicle that has been repaired and certified by a licensed repairer.
The vehicle must undergo a VIIU inspection before re-registration.
what_you_need: An AUVIS report (commonly known as a 'blue slip'), including identity, design, and safety checks
An Authorisation to Repair from TfNSW
A Certificate of Compliance issued by a licensed repairer
Original detailed receipts for all repairs carried out on the vehicle
For NSW written-off light vehicles: The required documentation listed above.

how_to_steps.text: Visit a Service NSW Centre with your payment and the required documentation.
Arrange a time for the VIIU inspection (metropolitan areas) or the VIIU will contact you to arrange a time (regional areas).

more_info.text: The VIIU carries out inspections of vehicles to confirm their identity.
If you've been given authorisation by Transport for NSW to repair a written-off vehicle, the VIIU will carry out the final inspection of the vehicle, prior to your applying for registration.

faqs.q: What must happen after a written-off light vehicle is repaired?
faqs.a: After being repaired and certified by a licensed repairer, the vehicle must undergo a VIIU inspection before it can be re-registered.

faqs.q: Do interstate written-off vehicles need special steps?
faqs.a: Yes, interstate written-off light vehicles must have been re-registered in another state or territory following the write-off event before they can be registered in NSW.

faqs.q: Where can I arrange the VIIU inspection?
faqs.a: In metropolitan areas, you should arrange a time for the VIIU inspection. In regional areas, the VIIU will contact you to arrange a time.
